- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by rapid decline (e.g., >80% from peak), apply downward correction of 5–10% to prevent overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days falling >2% from peak), model often fails to adjust; apply lagged correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast for next 2–3 periods.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.3) and model forecasts remain high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with sentiment-driven downward bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days); apply downward adjustment of 3–7% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model may misinterpret momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
